take_homes: Don't hand over the whole agent. Pick one of four things: the context, a skill, the output pushed to where they look, or an interface they pull from. Pick it based on what the teammate needs done, not on what fits our stack.
Rolling out access is not the same as people using it. Absorption takes weeks and someone has to answer for the agent, and I haven't named that person for the sales idea.
Ask one person how they do the job today before I build or show anything.

monday.move: Message one person in sales and ask for twenty minutes on how they do their pipeline prep today. Don't show them any agent. I'll also write the people plan for the sales idea and see whose name is missing.
monday.who: one sales lead. I'll have to pick the name, since nobody has asked for this.
monday.when: Monday morning for the message. The twenty minutes would be later that week.
monday.stop_condition: If they say the current spreadsheet and CRM already do the job and they wouldn't switch, I drop the weekend build.
monday.blocker: Nobody outside engineering asked for it, and I still don't know who will maintain it. I might also just build it anyway.

misconception.why: The module is about sharing and adoption and never gets to checking output. The scar story is about leadership not deciding, not about the agent's output being wrong. I skipped the 'read the file' checks and nothing made me regret it. Only the 'accountability doesn't copy' idea touched it, and only a little.

one_line: Good for thinking about rolling agents out to non-engineers, and the story is the best part, but the exercises are slow if you've already run agents.
